Pulse for 19 October 2026

The stories from 19 October 2026 in the Pulse of the Sapaude app, in our own words. Terms you don’t know are explained in the glossary. Glossary

AI agents

AI agents get a watchdog

Microsoft now tells companies to watch their own AI agents the way they would watch a new hire with access to everything, and it is selling the software to do it.

Device

AI apps switch chips easily

Most AI software is quietly tied to Nvidia's chips. Amazon now offers a way out that, the company says, needs just one changed line of setup.

New model

Cheap AI that often bluffs

MiniMax's new model M3.1 Flash reasons about as well as Google's fast model for a fraction of a dollar per task, yet independent testers found it almost never admits when it doesn't know an answer.

New model

AI pulls invoice data fast

Copying an order number or an invoice total out of an email is dull work that companies often leave to chatbots. Cloudflare has built a smaller AI model just for that job, and it says it is faster, cheaper and more reliable.

Everyday tool

AI videos now speak German

The AI video tool Kling can now produce half-minute clips in which people speak German, English or Spanish with matching lip movements, which brings short training and product videos within reach of anyone with a script.

AI agents

AI agents hacked 100+ sites

A single attacker let a swarm of AI agents break into company websites largely on their own, and the software that steered them is free for anyone.

Everyday tool

AI strips ads off your TV

Thousands of people are letting a coding assistant clean the ads and preinstalled clutter off their smart TVs, a sign of how far ordinary users can now get with an AI that takes actions.

New model

Agents run on your own PC

Nvidia has released new AI models that companies can run on their own servers and that work directly on a laptop, so your data doesn't have to leave the building.

AI agents

AI agents now shop for you

More and more people let an AI agent do their shopping, and the payment company Stripe now reports steep growth in purchases that software makes on someone's behalf.

AI agents

IT gets a grip on AI bots

Pax8, a marketplace through which IT service providers sell software to small businesses, has launched a control center meant to keep track of every AI agent a company uses, plus a ready-made AI coworker.

Study

AI rewrites ancient code

Banks and insurers still run on software written in programming languages older than most of their staff. OpenAI says its newest models have become far better at understanding and rewriting exactly that kind of code.
